result.topic_en: Riemann's calculations toward the Riemann–Siegel formula. They treat the asymptotic expansion of the phase $\vartheta(t)$, the functional equation of $\zeta(s)$ via $\Pi$ (the Gamma function), and an integral representation of $\sum e^{-mx}x^{s-1}/(e^x-1)$ evaluated by the saddle-point method. This leads to series in derivatives of an auxiliary function $f(s)=\int Z\,dz$.

methods.what: Asymptotic expansion of the Riemann–Siegel theta function
Splitting zeta into a finite Dirichlet sum plus an integral remainder
Expression of $e^{2\vartheta i}$ through Gamma values
Integral representation of the ratio $\cos(2s^2\pi+\frac38\pi)/\cos 2s\pi$ (Riemann–Siegel kernel)
Saddle-point expansion: Taylor expansion of the logarithm around the saddle point $\alpha$
Main term of the Riemann–Siegel formula
Derivatives of the auxiliary integral $f(s)$ as moments in $y$
